title: Planaria combine a messy mixoploid genome with highly reliable anatomy

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Planaria combine a messy mixoploid genome with highly reliable anatomy

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Because planaria reproduce by fission and regeneration and so retain somatic mutations, they have a very messy, mixoploid genome, yet they have highly reliable anatomy, with every fragment regenerating a normal worm.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Shreesha L 2023, Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model › 1. Introduction

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: As a result, planaria have an incredibly messy genome (indeed, worms are mixoploid—different numbers of chromosomes in each cell). Despite this, they have the most reliable anatomy: every fragment of a planarian regenerates a perfect worm each time.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Shreesha L, Levin M, “Cellular Competency during Development Alters Evolutionary Dynamics in an Artificial Embryogeny Model”, Entropy (Basel, Switzerland) (2023), doi:10.3390/e25010131; section “1. Introduction”. Scope: Asexual, fissiparous planarians (e.g. Schmidtea mediterranea asexual strain)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-competency-02: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.65

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Public planarian resources and literature can test genomic heterogeneity and regeneration robustness in subsets. They are unlikely to justify the absolute formulation across all fragments and conditions.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify cell-to-cell karyotype and sequence variation in fissiparous planaria and compile regeneration outcomes by fragment position and condition. The conjunction requires high genomic heterogeneity and consistently normal regenerated anatomy despite it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mixoploidy requires cell-resolved karyotype data not standard bulk sequencing.

Published regeneration reports under-sample failures and adverse conditions.

'Every fragment' is an overbroad universal.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
analysis feasibility: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.48
data existence: 0.68
operationalizability: 0.86
discriminating power: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Assemblies and PlanMine document a difficult Schmidtea genome, and many regeneration series report reliable restoration, but neither resource is a systematic census of chromosome number per cell or of every fragment. The two halves of the claim can be checked only by compiling biased published measurements. Coverage is a subset of fissiparous planarians, not the full stated scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compile chromosome-count distributions for fissiparous planarians and fragment-level regeneration outcomes from deposited genomes, PlanMine records and published karyotype and amputation series. Variable ploidy together with near-complete restoration of anatomy would support the claim; a stable karyotype, or frequent regeneration failure, would refute the corresponding half.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Mixoploidy is mostly cytogenetic and is scattered across papers rather than stored as a single count dataset.

Regeneration success is size- and species-dependent, so 'every fragment' is stronger than typical published series.
